I will still start from last year’s pattern, because on 30.4 mu I cannot afford to gamble with the whole farm. I have well irrigation, so I will keep wheat-maize as the main line and leave a smaller block for millet. I have enough experience to know that on our Quzhou land, yield comes first from getting the stand right, then from not letting fertilizer or water fall short at the key stages. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the crop run short in a dry spell or at jointing and grain filling. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, put the base fertilizer on firmly, irrigate three times if water is normal, and hold yield around 520 kg per mu. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a little strong, and do no-tillage seeding after wheat harvest to save time and catch soil moisture; with two irrigations I will aim for about 640 kg per mu. Millet is more for diversification and risk control, so I will keep it on a smaller area with lower fertilizer, one irrigation, lighter pesticide use, and aim around 300 kg per mu. I do not farm by theory alone; I look at cost, water, labor, and what has proved stable here, then I adjust a little, not wildly.
